rules.title: S.2983 – An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.requirement: Pending Senate bill that would prohibit algorithmic rent setting. Reported favorably by the Housing Committee on 3/12/2026 and sent to Senate Ways and Means; it is not law and the page does not show its operative text.
rules.key_value: pending ban on algorithmic rent setting
rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.review_note: Bill text not captured; specific prohibitions unknown.

rules.title: H.5222 – An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market
rules.requirement: Pending House bill on algorithmic rent fixing in rental housing. Reported favorably 3/12/2026 and sent to House Ways and Means; it is not law and its operative text is not shown.
rules.key_value: pending bill on algorithmic rent fixing
rules.quoted_span: An Act relative to preventing algorithmic rent fixing in the rental housing market

rules.title: State prohibition on local rent control (G.L. c. 40P)
rules.requirement: Massachusetts cities and towns may not enact, maintain or enforce rent control. Only a voluntary, municipally-compensated scheme limited to owners of 10+ units and low-rent units is allowed.
rules.key_value: Statewide ban on local rent control
rules.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.coverage_conditions: All cities and towns in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Voluntary, compensated regulation by accepting municipalities for owners of ten or more units and units with fair market rent of $400 or less.
rules.conflict_note: State bar may preempt local rent control ordinances in MA cities (e.g., Boston, Cambridge).

rules.title: Initiative Petition 25-21 – statewide rent increase cap (blocked from ballot)
rules.requirement: The proposed initiative would have repealed G.L. c. 40P and capped annual rent increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC ruled it cannot appear on the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law.
rules.key_value: lesser of CPI or 5% annual cap (not enacted)
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings with four or fewer units, units less than 10 years old, certain publicly regulated units, short-term rentals, educational/religious/nonprofit facilities.
rules.conflict_note: Proponents say defect is easily fixable and hint at a 2028 refiling; no rule in force.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment under a written lease
rules.requirement: For nonpayment under a written lease, a landlord may end the lease with 14 days' written notice to quit. The tenant can stop termination by paying all rent due with interest and costs by the answer day; late government subsidy payments require a hearing continuance of at least 7 days.
rules.key_value: 14 days' notice to quit; cure by paying rent, interest, costs
rules.quoted_span: Upon the neglect or refusal to pay the rent due under a written lease, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the lease
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.

rules.title: Notice to determine estate at will
rules.requirement: A tenancy at will ends with 3 months' written notice (or the rent interval/30 days if longer when rent is paid more often). For nonpayment, 14 days' notice to quit; a tenant without a similar notice in the prior 12 months can stop termination by paying all rent due within 10 days.
rules.key_value: 3 months' notice; 14 days for nonpayment; 10-day cure
rules.quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy;
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.

unverifiable_exemptions: tenancy must be at will (not a fixed-term lease)

rules.title: Reprisal protections for tenants
rules.requirement: A landlord may not threaten or take reprisals against a tenant for enforcing housing laws, reporting violations or joining a tenants' union. Liability is 1-3 months' rent or actual damages plus fees; a termination notice (except for nonpayment), rent increase or substantial change within six months is presumed a reprisal.
rules.quoted_span: shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.penalty: Damages of not less than one month's nor more than three months' rent, or actual damages if greater, plus costs and attorney's fees.

rules.title: Notice to quit for nonpayment: required state form
rules.requirement: A written notice to quit for nonpayment must be accompanied by a state form listing repayment agreements, rental assistance, court rules and eviction restrictions, with a statement that the notice is not an eviction. Courts will not accept a nonpayment summary process filing without proof the form was delivered.
rules.key_value: State form required with nonpayment notice to quit
rules.quoted_span: No court having jurisdiction over an action for summary process pursuant to chapter 239, including the Boston municipal court department, shall, in an eviction for nonpayment of rent for a residential dwelling unit, accept for filing a writ, summons or complaint without proof of delivery of the form required under this section

rules.title: Security deposit cap and handling (G.L. c. 186, § 15B)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not require a security deposit above the first month's rent. The deposit must be held in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts account with receipt and statement of condition, 5% annual interest (or bank rate if lower), and be returned within 30 days after the tenancy ends less itemized lawful deductions; violations risk forfeiture and treble damages.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent cap; return within 30 days; 5% interest
rules.quoted_span: a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2)
rules.effective_date_note: Original effective date not stated; 2025 amendment effective 2025-08-01 added agents and a possible fee in lieu of deposit.
rules.exemptions: Leases of 100 days or less for vacation or recreational purposes.
rules.penalty: Forfeiture of right to retain deposit; treble damages plus 5% interest, costs and attorney's fees.

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.title: Limit on upfront charges at lease start (G.L. c. 186, § 15B(1)(b))
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a landlord (or agent, from Aug 1, 2025) may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit of no more than one month's rent, and the cost of a key and lock. Application, screening and similar fees are not allowed for landlords.
rules.key_value: Only first, last, deposit (max 1 month), lock and key
rules.quoted_span: At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
rules.effective_date_note: Date the amendment extending the limit to agents took effect; the underlying limit on lessors predates it (secondary source says since the 1970s).
rules.exemptions: Vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less.

unverifiable_exemptions: vacation or recreational rentals of 100 days or less

rules.title: Broker fee allocation: only the party who engaged the broker pays
rules.requirement: A licensed broker or salesperson may contract with the tenant or the landlord, not both. Any fee must be paid only by the party who originally engaged the broker.
rules.key_value: Broker fee paid only by the party who hired the broker
rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson
rules.effective_date_note: Amended text effective August 1, 2025 per 2025, 9, Sec. 136.

rules.title: Licensed broker fee disclosure regulation
rules.requirement: Licensed brokers may charge prospective tenants fees but must give written notice of the fee amount, time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on a lease, signed by the applicant, at the first personal meeting.
rules.key_value: Written broker fee disclosure at first meeting
rules.quoted_span: the broker has to tell the applicant in writing the amount of the broker’s fee, the time and manner of payment, and whether it is contingent on the owner and applicant actually entering into a lease or rental agreement
rules.review_note: Described only in a secondary source.

rules.title: Anti-discrimination: public assistance and housing subsidy recipients
rules.requirement: Landlords and others offering rental accommodations may not discriminate against someone because they receive public assistance or a housing subsidy such as a voucher, or because of a program requirement. Other tenant-selection discrimination and inquiries based on protected classes are also barred.
rules.key_value: ban on discrimination against public assistance / housing subsidy recipients
rules.quoted_span: For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient
rules.effective_date_note: Document does not state an effective date.
rules.exemptions: Subsection 7 excludes a single apartment in a two-family dwelling occupied by the owner.

no_rule_findings.finding: Massachusetts has no rent cap: the statutory ban on rent control (G.L. c. 40P) remains, and the proposed statewide cap was blocked from the November 2026 ballot.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: The petition would have repealed the Commonwealth’s existing statutory ban on rent control, G.L. c. 40P, and replaced it with a statewide cap on annual rent increases for most residential rental units

parsed.notes: MA state only. Algorithmic rent-setting has only pending bills (S.2983, H.5222), no enacted law. D056 (803 CMR 5, CORI housing) is link-only and was not added as a rule.
